pool.text: The town of Dieppe was intermittently under control of England until this year.
Michel le Vasseur and his brother Thomas le Vasseur left Dieppe.
Three hundred colonists heading to New France departed from Dieppe.
Merchants of Dieppe and Rouen were granted a trade monopoly by Cardinal Richelieu.
Captain Thomas Lambert sailed from Dieppe to establish a trading post.
Dieppe lost thousands of its Huguenot citizens who fled abroad.
The town of Dieppe was largely destroyed by an Anglo-Dutch naval bombardment.
The Maire de Dieppe was N while the city enjoyed mayoral status.
Dieppe was popularised as a seaside resort following a royal visit.
Dieppe was occupied by German naval and army forces after the fall of France.
Allied soldiers landed at Dieppe in the hope of occupying the town.
Dieppe was liberated by soldiers from the 2nd Canadian Infantry Division.
Dieppe in New Brunswick received its present name in honour of the raid.
The casino in Dieppe was inaugurated in the presence of Robert Buron.
The Hôtel de Ville in Dieppe was completed.
The water tower in the Vertus district was built by architect Herbelin.
The water tower has been decorated with a polychrome fresco by Victor Vasarely.
The small municipal theater was listed in the supplementary inventory of historic monuments.
A new seaside resort containing an outdoor seawater swimming pool was inaugurated.
A member of the French Communist Party was elected in Dieppe.
